clue.text: Affected by inflation? Sell now, if confused!

explanation.surface: A panicky investor told to dump stock now that rising prices are hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about economic inflation; the definition means physically puffed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swollen has been blown up or distended, the physical kind of inflation rather than the economic.

explanation.surface: New graduates arrive in town for a relaxed day off.
explanation.definitionFit: The sabbath is the weekly day of rest, a day free from work.

clue.text: Professional sightseer?

setter's reading: a medical specialist whose job is examining eyesight

explanation.walkthrough: A sightseer sounds like a tourist; here it is someone who sees to people's sight.
explanation.definitionFit: This eye doctor studies and treats disorders of vision, so looking at sight is the profession.

clue.text: Falls and spills all over the place

blocks.note: something absent is not there

explanation.walkthrough: Edward's absence is read as not Ed.

clue.text: Blurts out: adding a note is less obvious

indicators.note: letters blurted out come tumbling forth in no particular order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks without thinking is, odd as it sounds, being subtler by adding a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: The added note E joins the anagram fodder before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle means delicate or hard to detect, so the comparative form is a direct synonym for less obvious.

clue.text: Speeds up manoeuvring round set points

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A driver accelerates while steering around the marked points of a course.

clue.text: German slang sounds like nonsense

explanation.surface: Remarking that German slang sounds like gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: Bosh is an old British word for nonsense; the answer is a wartime insult for a German soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Boche was a derogatory slang term used by French and British soldiers for Germans in the World Wars.

clue.text: Its members are all players in the City

clue.text: Others design to begin again

blocks.note: the rest are the others
design as a visual craft

explanation.surface: Other people draw up a plan to start over.

clue.text: Responsible for embarrassing outbursts out of sight

second meaning: working where the audience cannot see

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who causes public rows yet stays hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: To be behind something is to be responsible for it, and to make a scene is to cause an embarrassing outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre the area beyond the stage set is hidden from the audience, so the phrase means unseen or in private.

clue.text: Man hides in animal remains

he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man concealing himself inside a beast, as in some old ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal remains' looks like one phrase, but the split falls after 'animal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after burning, especially a cremated body, so they are remains.

clue.text: Deeds 'o man brought about her tragic end

definitions.text: Deeds 'o man brought about her tragic end

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: The actions of a man caused a woman's tragic death.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: in Shakespeare's Othello the heroine is smothered by her jealous husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is the wife whom Othello murders, so a man's deeds did bring about her tragic end.

clue.text: Waiting for the call

blocks.note: surface reading: awaiting a summons or vocation
setter's reading: staying on a telephone line until someone answers

explanation.walkthrough: The call sounds like a summons, but it is a phone call you stay on the line for.
explanation.definitionFit: On the telephone, staying connected while waiting to be put through is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Major reversed, followed by drunken binger talking incoherently

a drunk staggers about, so the following word is jumbled

blocks.note: major means large
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An army major in retreat and a drunk on a binge, both babbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like a military rank, but it is an adjective meaning large.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbering is jabbering in a fast, meaningless way, such as from fear or drink.

clue.text: Fire second before cry of derision

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a scornful shout

explanation.surface: Someone pulls the trigger a moment before being jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a gun is to shoot it; both verbs mean discharge a weapon.

clue.text: Spill a single drop!

blocks.note: surface reading: a warning not to waste any liquid
setter's reading: a woman letting one teardrop fall

explanation.walkthrough: The drop is not a liquid spilled from a glass but one from someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who weeps briefly lets one drop fall from her eye, a phrase used for showing emotion.

clue.text: Entrances, sounding like a blonde actress once

blocks.note: Diana Dors was a blonde British film star of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Describing a film star's grand arrivals on set.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was Britain's answer to Marilyn Monroe, a platinum blonde of 1950s cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors are the openings you pass through to enter a building or room, so they serve as entrances.

clue.text: Repudiates individual in Norfolk town

own as in individual or particular to oneself

explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge as one's own, which is to repudiate or reject.

clue.text: Pick of the field - compliment takes in many

explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a common yellow wildflower of meadows, something you might pick in a field.

clue.text: Their working day is spent behind the wheel

clue.text: Temporary abbreviation

blocks.note: first meaning: lasting only a little while
second meaning, read cryptically: a shortened word or phrase

clue.text: The whole orchestra express disapproval to it coming back

taken as written

clue.text: May have power

blocks.note: first meaning: the past form of the auxiliary verb may
second meaning: strength or force

explanation.walkthrough: May at the start looks like a name or month; it is the verb whose past tense is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is the past and conditional form of the modal verb, and as a noun it means strength or force.

clue.text: Head off girl turning right on time

explanation.surface: A driver avoids a collision by swerving right just in time.

clue.text: It sings out when it's time for tea
